narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Overcast conditions early will transition to mostly cloudy by midday, with temperatures climbing to a high of 27°C (81°F) and dropping to a low of 19°C (66°F) tonight. Thunder possible from the morning, peaking around midday. Winds will be north-northeasterly overnight, turning southwest by midday, with peak gusts reaching 38 km/h (21 kt). Afternoon showers and thunderstorms are expected with a 100% chance of rain delivering 34.4 mm (1.35 in), beginning between 16:00 and 17:00 before skies return to overcast in the evening. UV levels will reach a peak index of 9.2. Ground station air quality is highest at Dunga Beach with an AQI of 68. As of 06:01, reports through 05:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 21°C (70°F); low so far 20°C (68°F); peak sustained 9 km/h (5 kt); sky mostly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

Cooling through Saturday, with rain and thunderstorms likely Thursday, and rain and thunderstorms possible from Friday. Skies overcast throughout. Saturday's call: rain, 100%, with all four models wet; highs around 24°C (76°F). Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls it wet. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 87% of the time over 88 checks.

Further out, warming and becoming calmer through Wednesday, with showers and thunderstorms likely Sunday, Monday and Tuesday, and showers and thunderstorms possible Wednesday. Sunday: all four models wet, highs 26 to 28°C (78 to 82°F), thunder likely rather than possible. Monday: all four models wet, highs 25 to 28°C (78 to 83°F). Tuesday: all three models that reach it wet, highs 26 to 29°C (78 to 84°F).

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Monday. GFS is the wetter solution from Sunday to Monday; ECMWF, ICON and UKMO keep it drier. Wednesday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 28°C (82°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 90% of the time over 84 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Convective instability in the hours ahead: UKMO 3020 J/kg, ECMWF 2040 J/kg, GFS 1270 J/kg and ICON 960 J/kg. Thunder likely; any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above the 38 km/h (20 kt) forecast.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Peak gust 28 km/h (15 kt). Any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above this figure; the water is unsafe while one is nearby.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1012 hPa) and highest toward the southwest (1015 hPa) — a 4 hPa spread, a weak large-scale gradient. Pressure is also falling toward the northwest — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is rising. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across the basin's 5 points, pressure today sits between 1015.0 and 1016.9 hPa, rising by 1.6 hPa over three days. Pressure here over the last 24 hours: +0.0 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

On rain the record ranks ECMWF first at Day+3, right 87% of the last 30 checks and ECMWF first at Day+7, right 90% of the last 30 checks. On today's high GFS is the warmest model at 28.9°C (84.0°F) and ICON the coolest at 25.6°C (78.1°F); the call's 27.3°C (81.1°F) sits between them. At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others here yet. At Day+3, ECMWF is the strongest rain caller here and kenya_met the weakest. At Day+7, ECMWF is the strongest rain caller here and GFS the weakest.
